newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 13.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Market is seen regaining an upward bias following the Dow's substantial overnight rise after investors bet that the Federal Reserve would keep interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting meeting next week, traders said.
* But Sun Hung Kai Securities analyst Ramon Adviento says the main index will likely be jittery for the week moving in a band, with support at 2,600.
* Philippine markets were closed on Monday for local elections.
* On Friday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index slipped 10.71 points to 2,671.39.
* The Dow Jones ended up 123.22 points on Monday at 7,292.75.

* Commission on Elections chairman Bernardo Pardo said the local election was the most peaceful ever because there were no reports of death on election day. In the last village election in 1994, 26 people died.
* The Philippine Central Bank said it had agreed to temporarily exclude thrifts and savings banks from its earlier order setting a 20 percent limit on the exposure of banks to the real estate sector.
* Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson ruled out capital flight despite the recent fall in the local stock market adding that the peso is likely to remain stable.
* The Times Journal said that the Solid Group Inc and Sony Corp have formed a joint venture company that will handle the marketing and sales of Sony consumer audio-visual products.

* Megaworld Properties * Holdings Inc, Empire East & Land Holdings Inc and Filinvest Land Inc said late Friday that despite the scare of a possible crash in the local real estate market, they will forge ahead with projects.

* Manila Chronicle says three of the country's business tycoons - Enrique Zobel, Henry Sy Sr and Antonio Cojuangco -- have formed a real estate company that will develop a 180-hectare property in Calatagan, Batangas, south of Manila into a world-class residential resort complex.
* BusinessWorld said quoting Digital Telecommunications Phils Inc that entry of Bell Telecommunications Phils Inc as a nationwide telephone service provider will result in ruinous competition.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer reported that Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chairman Perfecto Yasay said the SEC in consultation with the U.S. Agency for International Development has started to draw up the framework for the trading of options and warrants in a separate exchange.

* The Manila Electric Co said it will reduce power rates for its commercial and industrial customers in June as a result of the 4.82 centavos per kilowatt-hour cut in National Power Corp rates approved by the Energy Regulatory Board last Friday.
* Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp (PSPC), a unit of the Royal Ductch/Shell group of companies, reduced most petroleum prices except diesel effective Saturday.
* The peso closed lower on Friday at 26.373 to the dollar vs 26.368
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was down to 11.28125 percent from 11.3125 percent.
